text:
maria: deploy-bot flagged release 2026.04.02 (artifact v3.2.1) during preflight. SBOM provenance missing (cosign attestation absent) and vuln-scan shows 1 medium transitive in libbar (CVE-2025-abc). Were in a US change window but team wants to avoid full rollback. thoughts?

deploy-bot: preflight-check: SBOM_PROVENANCE=ABSENT, COSIGN_ATTESTATION=NOT_FOUND. vuln-scan: 0 high, 1 medium (transitive), 3 low. release-policy: HOLD until provenance/sig or explicit exception.

tom: tagging @sana (security) and @josh (oncall). We can do a thin regional carveout (us-east small %) but infra needs an explicit exception token from security to proceed.

sana: quick assessment: CVE-2025-abc is a medium found in a transitive build-tool that does not ship in the runtime container. Exploitability appears limited, but I want evidentiary proof. Root cause looks like cosign attestation step failed in the publishing pipeline due to network timeout.

josh: Ops note: even if security ok's, k8s admission webhook requires signed SBOM for >=10% traffic. We can start a 1% warmup for 30m if security gives token.
maria: options: (A) manual cosign attach + re-scan then proceed to 1% for 30m, (B) pin to previous artifact v3.2.0 and delay, (C) timeboxed exception for 30m 1% with auto-rollback.

sana: I prefer A then C. Manual attestation is quick: `cosign attest --key k8s://projects/release-keys artifact-v3.2.1.tar.gz --type sbom` then re-run `vuln-scan`. If re-scan shows no new med/high, I will issue exception token for 30m 1%.

maria: doing manual attest now. cmd: 
```
COSIGN_KMS=kms://projects/prod/key cosign attest --type sbom artifact-v3.2.1.tar.gz
```

deploy-bot: cosign: FAILED (timeout). SBOM attestation still missing.

josh: network flakiness on the publisher side. I can retry from a different runner. Standby.

maria: reattempting from runner-42...

deploy-bot: cosign: OK 1f2b4ad attached. SBOM uploaded to gs://sboms/prod/2026-04-02/v3.2.1.sbom.json

maria: re-run vuln-scan: `./tools/vuln-scan --sbom gs://.../v3.2.1.sbom.json --output short`

deploy-bot: vuln-scan: 0 high, 0 medium, 2 low (both transitive). No new med/high.

sana: Security: issuing short-lived exception token `sec-exc-20260402-1` for 30 minutes at 1% in us-east. Conditions: immediate rollback on >3x baseline error-rate OR discovery of any new medium/high in subsequent scans. I will monitor live.

legal-bot: Legal notice: attach attestation line to release notes and create ticket REL-SEC-2026-456 for SBOM provenance audit within 5 business days.

josh: starting 1% warmup (us-east-1) with flag `warmup_v3_2_1=true`, start_ts=3610010200. Auto-rollback set to 30m (will cancel at 3610012000) unless triggers fire earlier.

deploy-bot: rollout: region us-east-1 traffic 1%, start_ts 3610010200. Monitoring hooks: 5xxs, p95 latency, inference checksum drift.

maria: monitoring dashboards up. oncall: @josh. I added the release note line: "Post-publish SBOM attestation attached; medium transitive CVE assessed non-shippable. Starting 1% us-east warmup for 30m under monitoring; SBOM audit ticket REL-SEC-2026-456 created."

sana: I'll revoke token immediately if anything looks off.

josh: 10m in, metrics look clean. no increase in 5xx or latency.

maria: 30m elapsed, no triggers. proceeding to ramp to 10% and then full rollout per release playbook. Closing hot exception. Will update REL-SEC-2026-456 with timeline and artifacts.

sana: closing from security side. Please keep the post-release audit notes.

maria: thanks everyone. tagging for record: cosign failure -> manual attest -> re-scan -> 1% warmup exception -> ramp. Learned: add retry logic to the cosign step in CI.

deploy-bot: rollout continued to 10% at 3610012400; thread will auto-archive in 7 days."
